current.text: He joined Milwaukee from Miami in the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade.

He is projected to start for Milwaukee, likely at forward because the power forward group is thin. The projected opening lineup is Rollins, Herro, Jaquez, Kuzma and Turner, and it could change by December or March.
Milwaukee's rotation is very unclear. The team has many guards fighting for minutes, and new coach Taylor Jenkins might use a deep rotation.
His assists should drop because Milwaukee has so many ball handlers.
Much of his production last season came when two or three Miami players were out, including Herro.
The expert does not trust his late-season shooting surge and sees little upside. He is fine only as a late flyer.

A trade is possible. He was called the Miami piece most likely to be moved before the season, possibly to Denver, and Milwaukee needs trades because Kuzma, Jaquez, Porter and Herro do not fit well together.
Milwaukee is expected to be a bad team, around 33 wins. It does not own its draft pick, so it has no reason to tank.
Yahoo lists him as questionable for rest.

durable.text: The experts rate him low. They see him at best as a sixth man, or a seventh or eighth man on a good team.
He needs opportunity and usage to produce fantasy value.
He gets few defensive stats. His steals and blocks are below average.
Threes are his weakest category for his position. A punt 3PM team loses little with him.
FG% and assists are his best categories. He shoots a good FG% on solid volume for a wing.

note: He is priced right at the edge of our draft pool (Yahoo rank 135 at 1.5 USD average cost, ESPN rank 148 at 1.2 USD). The experts see him only as a 1 USD late flyer, best suited to punt 3PM builds that want FG% and assists from a wing. Early in the season, check whether he holds the starting forward spot and keeps close to the 4.7 assists and 50.7 FG% of last season with Herro and Rollins handling the ball. Also watch for trade news.
